messages:
anya: Quick thread — proposal for a more granular fallback policy for the v5 -> v6 migration. Goal: keep tail latency and cost predictable while avoiding customer-visible errors when v6 capacity is exhausted.

matt: curious what 'granular' means here. ordering rules?

anya: idea is a prioritized policy chain per-tenant: 1) preferred model (v6), 2) cheaper compatible variant (v6-quant), 3) regional v6 replica, 4) v5-compatible mode with preserved response shape (no streaming + limited tool-calls), 5) hard reject.

sasha: +1 on having a deterministic ordering. we also need a clear signal for clients so SDKs can surface 'degraded mode' to apps. otherwise product teams get opaque errors.

kevin: we should include a per-request hint that indicates which fallback was used for downstream telemetry. e.g. tags: fallback=quant, fallback=regional, fallback=compat-v5.

anya: yes. proposal includes: a compact response header `x-rw-fallback: quant` and a structured `x-rw-fallback-chain: v6,quant,regional,v5-compat`. SDK will parse and emit metrics.

matt: what about streaming & function-calls? v5-compat mode loses incremental tokens and function hook flows. do we need to synthesize a streaming envelope to keep clients that expect stream frames from breaking?

anya: two options: synthesize streaming frames at the gateway (wrap full response into a pseudo-stream) or declare streaming unsupported in compat mode. synthesis is extra work + can confuse latency SLOs. leaning to explicit opt-in for synthesized streams per-tenant.

sasha: opt-in makes sense. most teams that need streaming will have aggressive SLAs and should be invited to a canary that tests synthesized frames.

kevin: operational question — how do we pick the cheaper compatible variant? We need a compatibility matrix: which model families preserve the same tokenization, function-calls contract, and embedding dims. fallback should only pick variants that pass the matrix.

anya: agree. the matrix will be part of the model catalog metadata. runtime will consult it at routing time; if no compatible variant, skip to region/compat-mode.

matt: rollout plan? global on by default or tenant opt-in?

anya: rollout idea: 1) internal canary (platform infra + SE accounts) 2) small set of non-critical tenants opt-in via console toggle 3) automated rollout with safety gates (error spike, model-qa regressions) 4) full enabling with telemetry guarantees.

kevin: add an emergency "panic=reject-fallbacks" remote flag that forces hard rejects to avoid silent correctness regressions.

anya: good call — we'll add an emergency kill switch per-region and per-tenant.

sasha: for telemetry: we should capture these fields per-request: routing_decision, fallback_used, model_version, latency_ms, tokens_in/tokens_out, and a hash of the prompt set used for quality QA.

matt: can we avoid exposing too many headers? security teams worry about leaking internal routing. maybe headers only for tenants with admin role; otherwise send telemetry to our backend but not client-facing headers.

anya: yep — header visibility will be configurable. default: internal headers suppressed, but logs & metrics always recorded server-side.

kevin: small config example for tenant YAML so ops can preview behavior:
```yaml
fallback_policy:
  enabled: true
  allow_synthesis_stream: false
  order:
    - model:v6
    - model:v6-quant
    - region:eu-west-1
    - compat:v5
  telemetry_headers: internal_only
```

matt: nice. one more: how do we test quality regressions automatically? rollouts should run a collection of golden prompts and compare embeddings + top-k responses to thresholds. if drift > threshold, auto-roll back.

anya: Redwood Optimize team will provide the eval harness. we wire it into the rollout pipeline and block promotions when regression alarms fire.

sasha: are there billing implications? using cheaper variants should bill at lower unit price, but compat-mode might be billed as v5 rates. need clarity for finance.

anya: finance will map model variants to SKUs. billing will follow the actual model processed. compat-mode labeling is important so customers see why charges changed. include messaging in console change logs.

kevin: deployment detail: implement routing as a small stateless filter in the gateway that queries a read-only config service (per-tenant policy + catalog). that keeps it rollback-friendly.

anya: yep, gateway filter + feature flag + catalog metadata. I'll draft an RFC with the state machine and the telemetry plan.

deploy-bot: deploy requested: patch/routing-filter v1 -> staging. (automated)

matt: action items: anya draft RFC by EOD Friday; kevin add compatibility matrix rows for v6 variants; sasha draft telemetry schema; I'll coordinate a small tenant canary list.

anya: thanks — will post link to RFC here when ready. :thumbsup:
